paragraphs.text: Drive the DeepSeek Harness sidebar browser itself: a visible pointer, real clicks and typing, upload
and download, site logins kept across sessions.
# dsh-inner-browser-use
A Chrome that the agent owns, mirrored into the right column of DeepSeek Harness.

The agent opens pages, reads them, clicks, types and scrolls. The browser is a separate
Chrome with

its own profile on disk, not the tab the product ships: the column shows a
live picture of that brow
ser, and your own cursor keeps working on the picture.
## Tools
| Tool | What it does |
| `browser_open` | Starts the browser (or reuses the running one) and opens an address. `headless: f

alse` shows a real window on the desktop instead. |
| `browser_view` | Returns the address, the titl

e, every control as `1 … 120`, and the visible text. |
| `browser_read` | Reads the page the way a p
erson does: one Markdown block of headings, paragraphs, lists and links, no controls. Far fewer toke
ns than a snapshot on long pages, and the links stay usable. Give it a `query` and only the sentence
s that answer it come back: BM25 over Readability-style blocks, then per-sentence scoring with headi
ng, position and link-density priors, idf-weighted coverage, MMR de-duplication and a character budg
et — 92% fewer tokens on a long page in the bench. A question the page cannot answer returns the nea
rest passages and says so instead of pasting the page (79% fewer tokens in the bench). When the tab
has no answer, the other tabs this chat holds are read in the same call and the answer comes back wi
th the tab it came from — one read instead of switch-and-read-again (90% fewer characters in the ben

ch); `across: false` stays on this tab. |
| `browser_find` | Finds words (or a regex) anywhere on th
e page: matching controls come back with a clickable number, matching text with its point, each sayi

ng whether it is on screen. |
| `browser_extract` | Returns the items a CSS selector matches, one co

mpact line each with its link, instead of the whole page. |
| `browser_click` | Clicks a numbered co
ntrol, or an `x`/`y` point. `double: true` double-clicks. A cookie banner or modal over the control

is cleared first, then the click happens. |
| `browser_type` | Types text into the focused field, or

clicks a numbered control first. Chinese goes in as one string. `submit: true` presses Enter. |

## The column

The pane is a picture of the browser, sent as JPEG over the session's own stream: quality 72,
every

frame, about 82 KB and 25 per second on a page at rest. The page is laid out at the size
of the colu
mn, so the picture fills the frame instead of sitting letterboxed inside it.
Two pointers live on that picture:

- **The black arrow** is the agent. It marks where its last click landed, and it moves the
moment a

new one is dispatched, without waiting for the page to repaint.
- **Your cursor** is the real one. H

overing, clicking, the wheel and keystrokes are sent to
the browser as real mouse and keyboard input

, so a site that rejects scripted clicks still
works. Moving your mouse never moves the black arrow.

The address row above the picture is an address bar: type an address and press Enter, or use
back, f
orward and reload. The field follows the page except while you are editing it.

Typing arrives two ways: composed text (Chinese, emoji, anything the input method produces)
lands as

one insertion, and keys arrive as themselves, so Backspace deletes one character on
the page.

The pane opens only in the session that asked for it. A tool call in another session drives
the same
browser without taking the column that someone else is reading.
## Logins

The profile is a directory of its own: `~/.dsh/inner-browser-use/chrome/default`. It sits
outside th

e product's browser storage, which is created per process and gone on restart, so a
sign-in here is
still there the next day.

- **Plugin reload.** A reload adopts the Chrome that is still running, with the page it was on.
- **

Harness restart.** The same directory is opened again, so cookies, `localStorage` and
passwords that

Chrome saved all survive.
- **Shutdown.** The browser is asked to close rather than killed, which i

s when Chrome writes
the last of its cookies.
## What it costs

Measured on the same machine, same fixture, same headless Chrome, against four
others: Playwright MC

P, Chrome DevTools MCP, Stagehand and browser-use — all on
their model-free paths, since a model cal

l would only measure inference. Idle RSS
**459–552 MB** (1265–1672), idle CPU **0.03–0.47 %** (36–51

%), a wake in
**0.39–0.59 s** instead of a 4.6–5.1 s restart, and the same page read as **2302
char

acters** instead of 5662–21396. With six tabs open it is **864–922 MB**, about
+2 MB per tab, still

four renderer processes and 0.9 % of a core idle (0.24 % once
the pages settle). A tab on a browser

that is already up costs a median of
**42–54 ms** end to end; inside `openTab` the tab start itself

is **20 ms**
(24–33 ms for browser-use's raw `new_page`). A screenshot takes **51 ms**, the
same 48–

71 ms all four pay — the cost is Chrome's own capture — and what comes
back is a path plus 223 chara

cters instead of the 100–383 KB of base64 they
inline. Cold start is the one place we do not lead: *

*840 ms** (701–936) against
Stagehand 760 and browser-use 713, because both own Chrome in-process.
`

npm run bench` and `npm run tabs` reproduce all of it; the five-way tables are in
`docs/BENCH.md` (五

un bench` and `npm run tabs` reproduce all of it; the five-way tables are in
`docs/BENCH.md` (五家对照).
## What it does not do

- **It does not touch your Chrome.** The browser runs from a separate profile with no
connection to

the window you are using.
- **The layout viewport is the column, nothing more.** Desktop layout, no

mobile emulation, no
touch emulation; a very narrow column is laid out narrow rather than zoomed out

.
- **One page at a time.** A link that opens a tab is followed — the mirror lands on the new
page a
nd the popup closes — so there is never a second page to choose between.
## Compatibility

| Harness | 0.2.0 or newer |
| Chrome | Google Chrome, Chromium or Canary, 112 or newer |
| Runtime

| Node 20 or newer |
| License | MIT |

Details in docs/COMPATIBILITY.md; how the halves connect in
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
